brief:
The user likes romantic comedies and has a strong interest in history, particularly World War II films. They enjoy learning why conflicts started, are open to documentaries, and describe themselves as a huge PBS fan. This supports an interest in historical context, rather than a confirmed general preference for conflict or combat movies. They recently watched Sherlock Holmes movies and Dunkirk, the latter on TV, but gave no explicit assessment of either.

They are not a big fan of movie musicals. They strongly dislike horror: they dislike Aliens, although they are unsure whether to classify it as horror or science-fiction horror. Being frightened and jumping out of their seat are not entertainment to them; they say they refuse to go to horror movies.

They have seen only parts of Wonder Woman on TV. They enjoyed its action and comedy, found Wonder Woman attractive, and liked her spunk and ability to take care of herself. They explicitly said they like assertive women.

The first Matrix interested them; they thought the second and third were substantially weaker. Although it sometimes seemed “weird for weird’s sake,” figuring out what was happening held their interest, and they appreciated its element of mystery.

Their position on The Shape of Water remains uncertain. They knew little about it, recalled it as highly rated, and thought it had won an Academy Award or two. They had not become interested at the time or seen many trailers, and found the title unusual. When the assistant asked whether more exposure would have led them to watch it, they answered only “Might have.” This was tentative openness, not a commitment or a clear dislike of the film.
